case.title: Triple-negative breast cancer in an Ashkenazi Jewish woman
case.brief:
Referral from oncology. A woman of 38, of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry, was diagnosed with a grade 3 triple-negative breast cancer at 37. Her mother had a high-grade serous ovarian cancer at 52 and died at 55. A maternal aunt had breast cancer at 45.

Panel testing found a heterozygous BRCA1 variant, NM_007294.4:c.68_69del p.(Glu23ValfsTer17). Her aunt has since been tested and carries it.
tasks: Work through the PVS1 decision tree on the variant’s page. Where is the premature stop, and is nonsense-mediated decay expected?
Look at the frequency by ancestry group in gnomAD. Why is the grpmax filtering allele frequency so much lower than the Ashkenazi Jewish frequency? Does BS1 or BA1 apply?
Classify the variant and sign it, then compare your answer with the ENIGMA expert panel’s. Note where the panel’s gene-specific rules differ from the general guidance.
Who else in the family should be offered testing?
case.source: The variant is NM_007294.4(BRCA1):c.68_69del (GRCh38 17-43124027-ACT-A, ClinGen allele CA003783). The sources are ClinVar VCV000017662 and the ClinGen ENIGMA BRCA1/2 VCEP’s classification in the Evidence Repository, checked in October 2026. The patient and family are fictional.

patients.ref: Case 2: an Ashkenazi Jewish woman with triple-negative breast cancer
patients.referral: Referred by oncology with triple-negative breast cancer at 37. Her mother had ovarian cancer.
patients.summary: She is 38 and was diagnosed with grade 3 triple-negative breast cancer at 37. Her mother had high-grade serous ovarian cancer at 52.
patients.familyHistory: Her mother, who was not tested, had ovarian cancer at 52 and died at 55. Her maternal aunt, now 61, had breast cancer at 45 and carries the variant. Her sister is well at 35 and has not been tested. Her father is well at 69.

panel.name: Inherited breast cancer and ovarian cancer

phenotypes.name: Breast carcinoma
phenotypes.note: Triple-negative (oestrogen, progesterone and HER2 receptors negative), diagnosed at 37

patients.notes: The patient and family are fictional, but the variant and the published evidence about it are real.

expected.source: ClinGen ENIGMA BRCA1 and BRCA2 expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository, specifications v1.0.0; ClinVar VCV000017662 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2024-06-11).

notes.PVS1: The frameshift leads to a premature stop early in the protein, in an exon that the panel counts as biologically relevant, and nonsense-mediated decay is expected. VEP’s NMD plugin calls it NMD-escaping, because the stop is so close to the start of the coding sequence, but the panel decided otherwise from the evidence.
notes.PS3: Met, because one calibrated functional study found that the protein behaves like the pathogenic controls (PMID 32546644).
notes.PM5: Met at a strong level under ENIGMA’s rule for premature stop codons. The frameshift begins in exon 2, but its new stop codon (codon 39) is in exon 3, where the panel’s clinical and functional data show that premature stops are pathogenic. PM5 usually means another missense change at the same residue, so ENIGMA is using it in a different way here.
notes.PM2: Not met, because the variant is present in gnomAD, mostly in Ashkenazi Jewish people. It is at about 4 in 1,000 of their alleles because of a founder effect.
notes.BS1: Not met by ENIGMA’s thresholds, which use the filtering allele frequency in gnomAD’s non-cancer subsets (v2.1 exomes and v3.1) and leave out founder populations. A frequency above 0.002% gives BS1_Supporting, above 0.01% gives BS1 and above 0.1% gives BA1. The Ashkenazi Jewish frequency reflects a founder effect, so it is left out, as it is from gnomAD’s grpmax. gnomAD v4.1 has no non-cancer subset and includes people with cancer, so its filtering allele frequency (0.0025% in European alleles) is not the one the panel’s thresholds were set for.
notes.BA1: Not met, because outside the Ashkenazi Jewish group the variant is far below ENIGMA’s threshold of 0.1%.
